about: What the chord sheet does with a song. `songs` are the songs these are made on, as the document hands them over: one entry for each text box that has words, with `row` the slide it is on (counted from 0), its words and its chords (each `at` counted along the whole text box, a line break being one), and for a blank slide one entry with no words and `blank` set (in the song `bare`, with no `element` either: a slide that has no text box, which Simple Presenter gives one when a chord is put there and an app that makes no text boxes leaves out; the id of the box it adds is its own to make, and stands here as a sentence in brackets). `rows`: the sheet's rows made of each song (a row for the name of a group, and one for each line of each text box). `wordStarts`, `stops`, `stopAt`: where the spot can stand. `walks`: where the arrow keys take it. `edits`, `typing`, `copyPaste`: for each thing done, what the document is ASKED (setChords: this text box now has these chords, each `at` along the whole box; setChordsAlone: this line of chords with no words now has these, by name; `joined`: it is one step of undo with the change before it) and the song afterwards. In all of them `row` in a spot is the sheet's row, and `row` in what is asked is the slide. Some strings hold characters that cannot be seen: U+200B and U+2001.
madeBy: tools/make-vectors/sheet.js, by running the functions of Simple Presenter's qml/ChordSheet.qml and qml/chordlayout.js themselves. Do not edit by hand: run it again.
